description: Error Monitor page — centralized error tracking and management across automation runs, providing filtering, status management, and fix workflow generation capabilities.

groups.name: Error Visibility and Awareness
groups.description: The Error Monitor page serves as a centralized hub where users gain immediate awareness of all errors detected across automation runs. Upon navigating to this page, users should quickly understand the overall error landscape through summary badges showing counts by severity level (critical, error, warning), an unresolved error count indicator, and an auto-refreshing list of error events. The page must convey the health of the automation system at a glance, so a user who just finished a batch of workflow runs can immediately see whether anything went wrong and how severe the issues are.

assertions.description: Users can identify they are on the Error Monitor page and see a heading that clearly communicates the purpose of this view as centralized error tracking
Users can see at-a-glance severity breakdown badges showing how many critical, error, and warning level issues exist, allowing them to immediately gauge the urgency of unresolved problems
Users can see the total count of unresolved errors prominently displayed, giving them a single number that represents the backlog of issues requiring attention
Users benefit from automatic periodic refreshing of error data so they do not need to manually reload the page to see newly detected errors during active automation runs

groups.name: Error Filtering and Search
groups.description: Users need powerful filtering capabilities to narrow down the error list to the specific issues they care about. This includes text-based search across error messages, types, log sources, and workflow names, as well as structured filters for severity levels (critical, error, warning, info, debug) and status categories (new, acknowledged, in_progress, resolved, ignored, recurring). The filter system should support combining multiple criteria and provide clear feedback about how many filters are active, with the ability to clear all filters at once. Users dealing with dozens or hundreds of errors need to quickly isolate the subset relevant to their current investigation.

assertions.description: Users can type free-text search queries to find errors matching specific patterns, error types, log source names, or workflow names, enabling rapid location of known issues
Users can filter the error list by severity level, selecting one or more of critical, error, warning, info, or debug to focus on errors at the appropriate urgency level
Users can filter errors by their triage status (new, acknowledged, in_progress, resolved, ignored, recurring) to separate actionable errors from those already being handled or dismissed
Users can toggle the filter panel open and closed, and see a visual indicator of how many filters are currently active so they know when results are being narrowed

groups.name: Error Triage and Status Management
groups.description: Once users have identified relevant errors, they need to triage them by changing their status. The workflow involves expanding an error to see its full message and stack trace, then marking it as acknowledged (someone is aware), resolved (the issue is fixed), or ignored (not actionable). This triage workflow is essential for teams managing automation reliability, as it prevents the same errors from being re-investigated and provides a clear record of which issues have been addressed. Users should also be able to generate fix workflows from errors to automatically address recurring problems.

assertions.description: Users can expand individual error entries to reveal full error details including the complete message, stack trace, context lines, and resolution notes, providing the information needed to diagnose the root cause
Users can mark new errors as acknowledged to signal that someone is aware of the issue and it does not need further immediate attention from the team
Users can mark errors as resolved when the underlying issue has been fixed, removing them from the active error queue and providing closure on investigated problems
Users can generate automated fix workflows from detected errors, leveraging the AI system to propose and execute remediation steps for recurring or complex error patterns

groups.name: Error Context and Metadata
groups.description: Each error entry should provide rich contextual information beyond just the error message. Users need to see which log source produced the error, which workflow was running when it occurred, the file path and line number if available, the timestamp, the occurrence count for recurring errors, and the current triage status. This metadata helps users correlate errors with specific automation runs and prioritize based on frequency and recency.

assertions.description: Users can identify which log source produced each error, allowing them to trace issues back to specific applications or services being monitored

target.label: Error item with log source metadata

assertions.description: Users can see the total count of displayed errors and whether filters are narrowing the view, providing orientation about what portion of the error landscape they are currently examining

When no errors match the current filters or no errors have been detected at all, users see a clear empty state message that distinguishes between no errors existing and no errors matching filters, with guidance on configuring log sources if needed

groups.name: Browser Errors Panel
groups.description: The Error Monitor page includes a collapsible Browser Errors panel that surfaces UI Bridge SDK browser-level errors. This panel shows a health status badge indicating whether the browser environment is healthy, degraded, or broken, along with a list of recent browser errors. Users can expand or collapse this panel to manage screen real estate while still having quick access to client-side error information that may not appear in server logs.

assertions.description: Users can see a clearly labeled Browser Errors panel section that distinguishes browser-level errors from server-side automation errors
Users can see a health status badge on the Browser Errors panel indicating the current state of the browser environment as healthy, degraded, or broken
Users can expand and collapse the Browser Errors panel to manage screen space, with the panel retaining its collapsed or expanded state
Users can see a list of recent browser errors within the expanded panel, providing visibility into client-side issues that may affect UI reliability

groups.name: Detected Patterns Display
groups.description: The Error Monitor identifies recurring error patterns and clusters them for display. Users can see detected pattern groups with type badges indicating the kind of pattern, frequency counts showing how often each pattern occurs, and the ability to select a pattern to filter the error list to only matching errors. This helps users prioritize systemic issues over one-off errors.

assertions.description: Users can see a Detected Patterns section that groups recurring errors into identifiable clusters for easier prioritization
Each detected pattern displays a type badge indicating the category of the pattern cluster, helping users quickly classify the nature of recurring issues
Each detected pattern shows a frequency count so users can gauge how often the pattern recurs and prioritize high-frequency issues
Users can select a detected pattern to filter the error list to only show errors matching that pattern, enabling focused investigation of systemic issues

groups.name: Error Item Expanded Details
groups.description: When a user expands an error item, they see a detailed view containing the full error message rendered in a code block for readability, the stack trace if available, context lines surrounding the error, resolution notes from previous triage, recurrence history, and action buttons including 'Open in Editor' to jump to the source file and 'Show context' to view surrounding code. This detailed view provides all information needed to diagnose and act on an error without leaving the Error Monitor page.

assertions.description: Users can see the full stack trace of an expanded error, rendered in a code block format for readability, enabling them to trace the error back to its origin in the codebase

target.label: Stack trace section in expanded error

assertions.description: Users can see context lines surrounding the error location, providing additional code context without needing to open the file separately
Users can click an 'Open in Editor' button to jump directly to the source file and line where the error occurred, streamlining the debugging workflow
Users can click a 'Show context' button to reveal surrounding code context for the error, providing additional diagnostic information inline
Users can see the recurrence history for an expanded error, showing how many times and when the error has previously occurred, aiding in prioritization of persistent issues

groups.name: Loading, Empty, and Error States
groups.description: The Error Monitor page handles various data-loading states gracefully. When data is being fetched, a loading spinner is displayed. When no errors exist, an empty state with a success icon communicates that no issues have been detected. When the page itself encounters an error loading data, an error state with an alert icon is shown. An auto-refresh indicator displays the refresh interval (e.g., 'Auto-refresh: 30s') so users know data will update automatically.

assertions.description: Users see a loading spinner while error data is being fetched, providing feedback that the page is actively retrieving information rather than being stuck or broken
When no errors have been detected, users see a clear empty state with a success icon and message indicating that no issues exist, distinguishing this from a loading or error state
When the Error Monitor itself fails to load data, users see an error state with an alert icon and message explaining what went wrong, rather than a blank or misleading display
Users can see an auto-refresh indicator showing the refresh interval (e.g., 'Auto-refresh: 30s'), confirming that the error list will update automatically without manual intervention

groups.name: Fix Errors Workflow Generation
groups.description: The Error Monitor includes a dedicated Fix Errors button (FixErrorsButton component) that allows users to generate automated fix workflows for selected or visible errors. When activated, this triggers the AI system to analyze the error patterns and propose remediation steps as a workflow that can be executed. This bridges the gap between error detection and resolution, enabling users to take action directly from the monitoring interface.

assertions.description: Users can see a prominent Fix Errors button that communicates the ability to generate automated remediation workflows from the current error set
When the Fix Errors button is activated, users receive feedback that a fix workflow is being generated, such as a loading state or progress indicator on the button
Users can see which errors will be included in the fix workflow, either through selection checkboxes or a clear indication that all visible/filtered errors will be addressed

target.label: Error selection indicator for fix workflow

groups.name: Per-Run Scope Indicator
groups.description: The Error Monitor supports scoping the error view to a specific task run. When scoped, a blue banner appears at the top of the error list showing the name of the task run being viewed, along with a clear button to remove the scope and return to the full error view. This allows users who navigated from a specific workflow run to see only the errors relevant to that run, reducing noise from unrelated errors.

assertions.description: When the error view is scoped to a specific task run, users see a prominent blue banner indicating which run they are viewing errors for
The scope banner displays the name of the specific task run, so users can confirm they are viewing the correct subset of errors
Users can click a clear button on the scope banner to remove the per-run filter and return to viewing all errors across all runs
The scope banner is visually distinct (blue background) from the rest of the page, making it immediately obvious that the error view is currently filtered to a specific run

states.name: Error List — Default View
states.description: Default state: error list visible with search bar and filter toggle. Filter panel is collapsed. Shows severity badges in header and error count in footer.

transitions.name: Open filter panel
transitions.description: Click the Filters button to expand severity and status filter options

transitions.name: Expand an error
transitions.description: Click an error row to expand it and show full message, stack trace, and triage actions

transitions.name: Search errors
transitions.description: Type in the search input to filter errors by text

states.name: Filter Panel Open
states.description: Filter panel expanded showing Severity and Status filter button groups. Users can toggle individual severity levels and statuses to narrow the error list.

transitions.name: Close filter panel
transitions.description: Click the Filters button again to collapse the filter options

transitions.name: Clear all filters
transitions.description: Click 'Clear all' to reset all filter selections and return to unfiltered list

states.name: Error Detail Expanded
states.description: An error row is expanded showing full message, optional stack trace, context lines, triage action buttons (Acknowledge, Mark Resolved, Ignore), and Open in Editor link.

transitions.name: Collapse error detail
transitions.description: Click the expanded error row again to collapse it

transitions.name: Acknowledge error
transitions.description: Mark a new error as acknowledged to signal awareness

transitions.name: Resolve error
transitions.description: Mark the error as resolved to remove it from the active queue

transitions.name: Ignore error
transitions.description: Dismiss the error as not actionable

states.name: Empty State — No Errors
states.description: No errors match current filters or no errors detected. Shows success icon with 'No Errors Detected' message and guidance.

transitions.name: Errors appear after refresh
transitions.description: Auto-refresh brings in new errors, transitioning from empty to list view
